[LLM] PowerShell copy masqueraded as Windows Terminal in %PROGRAMDATA% running 6202033.ps1 Installation High
Hunts the Windows-specific stage-2 chain of the axios RAT: plain-crypto-js's setup.js copies powershell.exe to %PROGRAMDATA%\wt.exe (mimicking Windows Terminal, which legitimately lives under \Program Files\WindowsApps), writes %TEMP%\6202033.vbs as a hidden launcher, and uses it to invoke %TEMP%\6202033.ps1 — a renamed-interpreter LOLbin pattern that bypasses powershell.exe-named telemetry. Rationale: Microsoft's real Windows Terminal (wt.exe) ships only under \Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_* — a wt.exe under \ProgramData\ is the exact masquerade described in the article. Pairing that with the literal 6202033 token (used as the URI path on the C2 and as the .vbs/.ps1 filename basename) and node.exe parents with plain-crypto-js/sfrclak strings keeps this scoped to the actual dropper chain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/axios-compromised-on-npm-malicious-versions-drop-remote-access-trojan • https://socket.dev/blog/axios-npm-package-compromised
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1059.001 T1059.005 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath startswith @"C:\ProgramData" and FileName =~ "wt.exe")
   or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith @"C:\ProgramData" and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "wt.exe")
   or (FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "6202033")
   or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wt.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "6202033.ps1")
   or (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd") and FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("6202033","plain-crypto-js","sfrclak") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("plain-crypto-js","setup.js")))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentFile = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildFile = FileName,
          ChildPath = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where EventID == 4688
 | where (NewProcessName endswith @"\ProgramData\wt.exe")
    or (ParentProcessName endswith @"\ProgramData\wt.exe")
    or (NewProcessName endswith @"\wscript.exe" and CommandLine has "6202033")
    or (NewProcessName endswith @"\cscript.exe" and CommandLine has "6202033")
    or ((NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has "6202033.ps1")
    or (ParentProcessName endswith @"\node.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("6202033","plain-crypto-js","sfrclak"))
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType),
(ImProcessCreate
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where (TargetProcessName endswith @"\ProgramData\wt.exe")
    or (ParentProcessName endswith @"\ProgramData\wt.exe")
    or (TargetProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") and TargetProcessCommandLine has "6202033")
    or (TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and TargetProcessCommandLine has "6202033.ps1")
    or (ParentProcessName has "node.exe" and TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("6202033","plain-crypto-js","sfrclak"))
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: axios RAT Stage-2 — PowerShell Masqueraded as wt.exe in %PROGRAMDATA%
id: d3fab6e4-9a5f-4c02-b3d7-fab9e1c8d5f6
status: experimental
description: Detects the Windows stage-2 of the axios npm supply-chain RAT — PowerShell.exe copied to %PROGRAMDATA%\wt.exe (masquerading as Windows Terminal) and/or wscript/cscript launching the 6202033.vbs / 6202033.ps1 payload pair.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/axios-npm-compromised-maintainer-hijacked-rat
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/axios-compromised-on-npm-malicious-versions-drop-remote-access-trojan
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/13
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1059.005
  - attack.t1218
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_wt_image:
    Image|endswith: '\ProgramData\wt.exe'
  selection_wt_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\ProgramData\wt.exe'
  selection_vbs_token:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '6202033'
  selection_ps1_token:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '6202033.ps1'
  selection_node_dropper:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\node.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '6202033'
      - 'plain-crypto-js'
      - 'sfrclak'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - The legitimate Microsoft Windows Terminal binary is named wt.exe but resides under \Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_*\ — not under \ProgramData\. Any wt.exe in \ProgramData\ is suspicious.
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) AND ((@Image:(*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe OR *\\ProgramData\\WT.exe OR *\\ProgramData\\WT.EXE) OR @ParentImage:(*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe OR *\\ProgramData\\WT.exe OR *\\ProgramData\\WT.EXE) OR @NewProcessName:(*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe OR *\\ProgramData\\WT.exe)) OR (@Image:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\WSCRIPT.EXE OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe OR *\\CSCRIPT.EXE) AND @CommandLine:*6202033*) OR (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\pwsh.EXE) AND @CommandLine:*6202033.ps1*) OR (@ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*6202033* OR *plain-crypto-js* OR *sfrclak*)))
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_path="*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") AND (Processes.process="*6202033.vbs*" OR Processes.process="*\\Temp\\6202033*")) OR (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wt.exe") AND Processes.process="*6202033.ps1*") OR (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd") AND Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe") AND (Processes.process="*6202033*" OR Processes.process="*plain-crypto-js*" OR Processes.process="*sfrclak*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process_path Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.process_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_path="*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") AND (Processes.process="*6202033.vbs*" OR Processes.process="*\\Temp\\6202033*")) OR (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wt.exe") AND Processes.process="*6202033.ps1*") OR (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd") AND Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe") AND (Processes.process="*6202033*" OR Processes.process="*plain-crypto-js*" OR Processes.process="*sfrclak*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process_path Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.process_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access

            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

            - '\Cookies'

level: high

status: experimental

references:

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "ed8560c1ac7ceb6983ba995124d5917dc1a00288912387a6389296637d5f815c", "f7d335205b8d7b20208fb3ef93ee6dc817905dc3ae0c10a0b164f4e7d07121cd", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or SHA1 in~ ("92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "ed8560c1ac7ceb6983ba995124d5917dc1a00288912387a6389296637d5f815c", "f7d335205b8d7b20208fb3ef93ee6dc817905dc3ae0c10a0b164f4e7d07121cd", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or MD5 in~ ("92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "ed8560c1ac7ceb6983ba995124d5917dc1a00288912387a6389296637d5f815c", "f7d335205b8d7b20208fb3ef93ee6dc817905dc3ae0c10a0b164f4e7d07121cd", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "ed8560c1ac7ceb6983ba995124d5917dc1a00288912387a6389296637d5f815c", "f7d335205b8d7b20208fb3ef93ee6dc817905dc3ae0c10a0b164f4e7d07121cd", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or SHA1 in~ ("92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "ed8560c1ac7ceb6983ba995124d5917dc1a00288912387a6389296637d5f815c", "f7d335205b8d7b20208fb3ef93ee6dc817905dc3ae0c10a0b164f4e7d07121cd", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or MD5 in~ ("92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "ed8560c1ac7ceb6983ba995124d5917dc1a00288912387a6389296637d5f815c", "f7d335205b8d7b20208fb3ef93ee6dc817905dc3ae0c10a0b164f4e7d07121cd", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "ed8560c1ac7ceb6983ba995124d5917dc1a00288912387a6389296637d5f815c", "f7d335205b8d7b20208fb3ef93ee6dc817905dc3ae0c10a0b164f4e7d07121cd", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Article-specific behavioural hunt — axios compromised on npm: maintainer account hijacked, RAT deployed Exploitation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — axios compromised on npm: maintainer account hijacked, RAT deployed
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("setup.js", "wt.exe", "6202033.vbs", "6202033.ps1", "safe-chain.sh"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/dev/null", "/Library/Caches/com.apple.act.mond", "/tmp/ld.py") or FileName in~ ("setup.js", "wt.exe", "6202033.vbs", "6202033.ps1", "safe-chain.sh"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ENDPOINT

Hunts the two TeamPCP-published malicious telnyx wheels by SHA256 across Defender, Sentinel, and endpoint file telemetry. Pure IOC hit — fires the moment a developer or CI runner installs the backdoored package. Rationale: Both SHA256 hashes are published directly in Aikido's IOC list; matching them is unambiguous. The fallback path-match on telnyx/_client.py catches the case where pip extracts the wheel and the hash hits the cache before EDR scans the wheel itself. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/telnyx-pypi-compromised-teampcp-canisterworm
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 in ("7321caa303fe96ded0492c747d2f353c4f7d17185656fe292ab0a59e2bd0b8d9","cd08115806662469bbedec4b03f8427b97c8a4b3bc1442dc18b72b4e19395fe3")
   or (FolderPath has @"\telnyx\" and FileName =~ "_client.py")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileOriginUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileSHA256 in ("7321caa303fe96ded0492c747d2f353c4f7d17185656fe292ab0a59e2bd0b8d9","cd08115806662469bbedec4b03f8427b97c8a4b3bc1442dc18b72b4e19395fe3")
   or (TargetFilePath has @"\telnyx\" and TargetFileName =~ "_client.py")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256

[LLM] TeamPCP C2 egress to 83.142.209.203:8080 (telnyx WAV-stego dropper) Command & Control High
Hunts any host-initiated TCP connection to TeamPCP's hard-coded C2 IP on port 8080. This is where both the Windows hangup.wav and Linux/Mac ringtone.wav payloads are fetched from and where AES-encrypted tpcp.tar.gz bundles are POSTed back. Rationale: 83.142.209.203 is the sole C2 IP listed in Aikido's IOC block and serves both the Windows and Linux dropper as well as the exfil channel. Any outbound to this address from a non-sandbox host is a high-fidelity supply-chain compromise indicator. [LLM] TeamPCP WAV-stego payload drop (hangup.wav / ringtone.wav) Delivery High
Detects creation of hangup.wav or ringtone.wav files on disk that were sourced from C2 IP 83.142.209.203, the WAV-steganography carriers TeamPCP uses to deliver the second-stage executable (Windows) or Python script (Linux/Mac). Rationale: Aikido names the two specific filenames (hangup.wav, ringtone.wav) served from 83.142.209.203:8080. Correlating the filename with the C2-IP origin or a near-simultaneous network connect from the same host eliminates the FP risk of legitimate SIP/UC apps writing similarly-named ringtone assets. [LLM] TeamPCP msbuild.exe persistence in user Startup folder Installation High
Detects creation of a file named msbuild.exe under the per-user Startup folder %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup, the renamed-binary persistence TeamPCP uses on Windows. Legitimate msbuild.exe lives under Program Files, never in Startup, making the path the high-fidelity signal. Rationale: The Aikido article explicitly names %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\msbuild.exe and its .lock companion as the persistence artefacts. Genuine msbuild.exe never lives in a user's Startup folder, so the path itself is the discriminator. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/telnyx-pypi-compromised-teampcp-canisterworm

[LLM] TeamPCP Linux/Mac stdin-piped Python second stage (sys.executable -) Exploitation Medium
Hunts the Linux/macOS branch of the telnyx backdoor: _client.py base64-decodes a script and runs it via sys.executable with '-' as the argument, piping the third-stage collector to stdin. The 'python3 -' or 'python -' invocation with no script file from a non-interactive parent is the article-specific behavioural signature. Rationale: Article states the Linux/Mac branch 'runs it via sys.executable - piped to stdin' from the base64 blob at telnyx/_client.py line 459. python being its own parent and being invoked with a bare '-' is a very rare shape; combined with a same-host hit on the named C2 it becomes high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/telnyx-pypi-compromised-teampcp-canisterworm
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1140

let PyExecDash = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName matches regex @"^python[0-9.]*$"
  | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\bpython[0-9.]*\s+-\s*$"
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^python[0-9.]*$"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath;
let C2Hit = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteIP == "83.142.209.203"
  | summarize ConnTime = min(Timestamp) by DeviceName;
PyExecDash
| join kind=inner C2Hit on DeviceName
| where abs(datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, ConnTime)) <= 15
| order by Timestamp desc
let PyExecDash = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)^python[0-9.]*$"
  | where TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\bpython[0-9.]*\s+-\s*$"
  | where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)^python[0-9.]*$"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine;
let C2Hit = ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstIpAddr == "83.142.209.203"
  | summarize ConnTime = min(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname;
PyExecDash
| join kind=inner C2Hit on DvcHostname
| where abs(datetime_diff('minute', TimeGenerated, ConnTime)) <= 15

[LLM] TeamPCP tpcp.tar.gz exfil POST signature on egress proxy / WAF Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the exfiltration leg of the telnyx backdoor: an HTTP POST to 83.142.209.203:8080 carrying the X-Filename: tpcp.tar.gz header or a body referencing the same filename. Proxy / WAF / CommonSecurityLog telemetry catches the egress even when the host EDR did not see the WAV drop (e.g. unmanaged dev laptop on corp network). Rationale: Aikido explicitly names the exfil header X-Filename: tpcp.tar.gz, destination 83.142.209.203:8080, and POST method. Three independent IOCs in one query make this near-zero FP; the WAF/proxy variant catches even unmanaged endpoints. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/telnyx-pypi-compromised-teampcp-canisterworm
ATT&CKT1041 T1567
Data sourcesWeb.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "83.142.209.203" and RemotePort == 8080
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "tpcp.tar.gz"
    | project DeviceName, ExfilTime = Timestamp, FolderPath, FileName
  ) on DeviceName
| where isnotempty(ExfilTime) or InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^python[0-9.]*(\.exe)?$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ExfilTime, FolderPath, FileName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where DestinationIP == "83.142.209.203" or RequestURL has "83.142.209.203"
   | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
   | where FileName =~ "tpcp.tar.gz" or RequestURL has "tpcp.tar.gz" or Message has "tpcp.tar.gz"
   | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, FileName, Message, DeviceAction),
  (ImWebSession
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where DstIpAddr == "83.142.209.203" or Url has "83.142.209.203"
   | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
   | where FileName =~ "tpcp.tar.gz" or Url has "tpcp.tar.gz"
   | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, HttpMethod, Url, FileName, ThreatName, DvcAction)

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33634")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33634")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-33634")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-33634")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

DeviceProcessEvents

| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")

   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"

    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when

            - '\mshta.exe'

Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7321caa303fe96ded0492c747d2f353c4f7d17185656fe292ab0a59e2bd0b8d9", "cd08115806662469bbedec4b03f8427b97c8a4b3bc1442dc18b72b4e19395fe3") or SHA1 in~ ("7321caa303fe96ded0492c747d2f353c4f7d17185656fe292ab0a59e2bd0b8d9", "cd08115806662469bbedec4b03f8427b97c8a4b3bc1442dc18b72b4e19395fe3") or MD5 in~ ("7321caa303fe96ded0492c747d2f353c4f7d17185656fe292ab0a59e2bd0b8d9", "cd08115806662469bbedec4b03f8427b97c8a4b3bc1442dc18b72b4e19395fe3")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7321caa303fe96ded0492c747d2f353c4f7d17185656fe292ab0a59e2bd0b8d9", "cd08115806662469bbedec4b03f8427b97c8a4b3bc1442dc18b72b4e19395fe3") or SHA1 in~ ("7321caa303fe96ded0492c747d2f353c4f7d17185656fe292ab0a59e2bd0b8d9", "cd08115806662469bbedec4b03f8427b97c8a4b3bc1442dc18b72b4e19395fe3") or MD5 in~ ("7321caa303fe96ded0492c747d2f353c4f7d17185656fe292ab0a59e2bd0b8d9", "cd08115806662469bbedec4b03f8427b97c8a4b3bc1442dc18b72b4e19395fe3")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["7321caa303fe96ded0492c747d2f353c4f7d17185656fe292ab0a59e2bd0b8d9", "cd08115806662469bbedec4b03f8427b97c8a4b3bc1442dc18b72b4e19395fe3"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Silver Fox Japan tax-season lure: inbound email with Japanese HR/ESOP subject + gofile.io URL or RAR/ZIP · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)

[LLM] Silver Fox Japan tax-season lure: inbound email with Japanese HR/ESOP subject + gofile.io URL or RAR/ZIP Delivery High
Hunts the specific Silver Fox tax-season campaign against Japanese firms by joining inbound email with Japanese tax/HR/ESOP keyword subjects to either a gofile.io download URL or a RAR/ZIP attachment. Article explicitly names these subject patterns and gofile.io as the file hosting abused. Rationale: Subject fragments are pulled verbatim from the article's listed lures; gofile.io and WeTransfer are the hosting services the article explicitly calls out as red flags. Cross-checked with Sekoia's 'Silver Fox: only tax audit where the fine print installs malware' analysis and Hacker News' Oct-2025 Japan/Malaysia coverage which confirm the same lure shape and archive-based delivery for this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/silver-fox-the-only-tax-audit-where-the-fine-print-installs-malware/ • https://thehackernews.com/2025/10/silver-fox-expands-winos-40-attacks-to.html • https://www.rescana.com/post/silver-fox-expands-winos-4-0-valleyrat-and-holdinghands-rat-cyber-attacks-to-japan-and-malaysia

let ArchiveTypes = dynamic(["rar","zip","RAR","ZIP","7z","7Z"]);

union UrlSide, AttachSide

[LLM] gofile.io archive download by browser followed by extracted-EXE execution within 30 minutes Installation Medium
Correlates a file pulled from gofile.io by a browser/Outlook to a subsequent unsigned-or-temp-path executable launch on the same host within 30 minutes. Article calls out gofile.io as Silver Fox's chosen drop site and notes the payload is delivered inside RAR/ZIP archives, so this catches the post-click stage even when the email itself slipped past the gateway. Rationale: Article explicitly names gofile.io and WeTransfer as the hosting services Silver Fox abuses for the Japan tax-season campaign, plus calls out RAR/ZIP archives as the carrier. The 30-minute correlation window + extraction-tool parent set turns the broad 'file from gofile.io' signal into a high-fidelity post-extraction execution alert. Cross-checked Dark Lab and Sekoia ValleyRAT campaign write-ups which confirm the gofile.io / archive pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.darklab.hk/2026/03/25/silver-foxs-dual-pronged-strategy-dissecting-the-valleyrat-distribution-campaign/ • https://blog.sekoia.io/silver-fox-the-only-tax-audit-where-the-fine-print-installs-malware/

[LLM] ValleyRAT registry-resident shellcode (HKCU\Console\0|1) and MyPythonApp Run-key persistence Installation High
Hunts the ValleyRAT family persistence and shellcode-storage artefacts that Silver Fox deploys after initial execution: a value named d33f351a4aeea5e608853d1a56661059 written into HKCU\Console\0 or HKCU\Console\1 (encrypted shellcode store), and the MyPythonApp Run-key persistence value. Single-event detection — high signal because both names are unique to ValleyRAT. Rationale: Article confirms ValleyRAT (Win64/Valley) is the payload Silver Fox drops in this Japan tax-season campaign. The two registry indicators - HKCU\Console\{0,1} value d33f351a4aeea5e608853d1a56661059 and Run-key value MyPythonApp - are family-level ValleyRAT artefacts documented by Zscaler ThreatLabz and Fortinet FortiGuard, so a hit means a ValleyRAT install regardless of which Silver Fox sub-campaign delivered it. Cross-checked against: • https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/security-research/technical-analysis-latest-variant-valleyrat • https://www.fortinet.com/blog/threat-research/valleyrat-campaign-targeting-chinese-speakers • https://any.run/malware-trends/valleyrat/

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url

| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;

    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents

          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")

| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental

    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")

How a Poisoned Security Scanner Became the Key to Backdooring LiteLLM

Snyk
2026-03-24 14 use cases 6 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On March 24, 2026, threat actor known as TeamPCP published backdoored versions of the litellm Python package after stealing PyPI credentials via a compromised Trivy GitHub Action in LiteLLM's CI/CD pipeline. Here's what happened, how the three-stage malware works, and how to check if you're affected.

IPs83.142.209.11

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Malicious litellm 1.82.7/1.82.8 wheel install drops litellm_init.pth in site-packages · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — How a Poisoned Security Scanner Became the Key to Backdooring LiteLLM
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Python .pth startup hook executes subprocess to curl C2 (litellm fork-bomb pattern) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS / HTTPS egress to TeamPCP exfil infra (models.litellm.cloud, checkmarx.zone) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Exfil staging artefacts: session.key, payload.enc, session.key.enc, tpcp.tar.gz in temp · [LLM] TeamPCP Linux credential harvest: Python reading /etc/shadow + auth.log + cloud · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Malicious litellm 1.82.7/1.82.8 wheel install drops litellm_init.pth in site-packages Delivery High
Detects installation of the trojanized litellm PyPI versions 1.82.7 or 1.82.8 by spotting the diagnostic file litellm_init.pth being written into a Python site-packages directory (an unusual artefact name for legitimate packages) and/or pip writing litellm-1.82.7/litellm-1.82.8 .dist-info metadata. Versions 1.82.6 and earlier are clean. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit artefact litellm_init.pth (34,628 bytes) dropped into site-packages and the two malicious wheel versions 1.82.7 / 1.82.8. The file name is novel to this campaign and the dist-info paths are version-pinned, giving high fidelity. Cross-checked: PyPI advisory SNYK-PYTHON-LITELLM-15762713 and the FutureSearch disclosure both confirm the file name and sizes. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-PYTHON-LITELLM-15762713 • https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/24518
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546.018
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName =~ "litellm_init.pth" and FolderPath has "site-packages")
   or (FolderPath has_any ("litellm-1.82.7.dist-info", "litellm-1.82.8.dist-info"))
   or (FileName =~ "litellm_init.pth" and FileSize between (30000 .. 40000))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Facility in ("auth", "daemon", "user") or isnotempty(SyslogMessage)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("litellm_init.pth", "litellm-1.82.7.dist-info", "litellm-1.82.8.dist-info", "litellm-1.82.7-py3", "litellm-1.82.8-py3")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Python .pth startup hook executes subprocess to curl C2 (litellm fork-bomb pattern) Installation High
Detects the .pth-triggered execution chain unique to litellm 1.82.8: python(1) spawning python(2) (because the .pth re-fires on each interpreter), which in turn spawns curl or openssl to package and POST tpcp.tar.gz to models.litellm.cloud. The python→python→curl/openssl tree is what produced the RAM-exhaustion symptom McMahon reported. Rationale: Article-specific anchors: (a) python parent — because the .pth fires from the interpreter, (b) curl/openssl/tar child — the verbatim exfil stack named in the article, (c) the literal strings models.litellm.cloud, tpcp.tar.gz, session.key.enc, payload.enc. Generic python-spawns-curl is too noisy; the three IOC strings give the article-specific lift. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/poisoned-security-scanner-backdooring-litellm/ • https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/24518

| where (FileName in~ ("curl","curl.exe","openssl","openssl.exe","tar","tar.exe"))
   and (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("models.litellm.cloud","tpcp.tar.gz","session.key","payload.enc","session.key.enc")
        or ProcessCommandLine has "AES-256-CBC" and ProcessCommandLine has "-pbkdf2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,

| where SyslogMessage has_any ("curl","openssl","python")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, ProcessID, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DNS / HTTPS egress to TeamPCP exfil infra (models.litellm.cloud, checkmarx.zone) Command & Control High
Detects any host in the org resolving or connecting to the two TeamPCP-controlled exfil domains used across the litellm, Trivy, and Checkmarx KICS operations. Both domains were registered in March 2026 (models.litellm.cloud on Mar 23) — any resolution within or after that window is highly suspicious. Rationale: Direct IOC match on the exfil and C2 domains/IP that Wiz, Endor Labs, and Snyk all corroborate (same RSA key fingerprint across litellm/Trivy/KICS payloads). These domains have no benign legitimate use — registered Mar 23 2026 specifically for this campaign — so any hit is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/poisoned-security-scanner-backdooring-litellm/ • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/teampcp • https://www.wiz.io/blog/teampcp-supply-chain

)

),
( ImDnsActivity

[LLM] Exfil staging artefacts: session.key, payload.enc, session.key.enc, tpcp.tar.gz in temp Actions on Objectives High
Detects the four staging files the TeamPCP payload creates in the system temp directory while building the encrypted exfil bundle (AES-256-CBC session key wrapped with their RSA-4096 OAEP public key, archived as tpcp.tar.gz). All four names are hardcoded in the malware and shared across litellm / Trivy / KICS operations. Rationale: All four filenames (tpcp.tar.gz, session.key, payload.enc, session.key.enc) are quoted verbatim from the article's Stage 2 description. Wiz confirmed identical RSA public key across litellm/Trivy/KICS, meaning these staging names are reused across all three campaigns — extremely low FP rate. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/poisoned-security-scanner-backdooring-litellm/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/teampcp-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1560.001 T1486

| where FileName in~ ("tpcp.tar.gz","session.key","session.key.enc","payload.enc")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp),
            Files=make_set(FileName), DistinctFiles=dcount(FileName),
            Procs=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            CmdLines=make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            Paths=make_set(FolderPath)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where DistinctFiles >= 2 or array_index_of(Files, "tpcp.tar.gz") >= 0
| order by FirstSeen desc
Syslog

| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, ProcessID, SyslogMessage
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated),
            Procs=make_set(ProcessName), MsgSample=any(SyslogMessage),
            Hits=count()
          by Computer, HostName
| order by FirstSeen desc

[LLM] TeamPCP Linux credential harvest: Python reading /etc/shadow + auth.log + cloud Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the Stage 1 collection behaviour: a python process opening a high-fan-out set of sensitive Linux credential stores (/etc/shadow, /var/log/auth.log, ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, ~/.azure/, ~/.config/gcloud/, ~/.kube/, ~/.docker/config.json, .env, cryptocurrency wallets) within a short window — characteristic of the litellm 1.82.7/1.82.8 grabber, not a normal interpreter session. Rationale: The article lists the exact files/paths the Stage 1 grabber touches; we anchor on that high-fan-out set (≥3 distinct sensitive paths from a python interpreter within 7d) rather than any single path, which avoids generic /etc/shadow noise from sysadmins. The IMDS string 169.254.169.254 is included because the article explicitly calls out direct IMDS queries. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/poisoned-security-scanner-backdooring-litellm/
ATT&CKT1003.008 T1552.001 T1552.004 T1552.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let SensitivePaths = dynamic([
    "/etc/shadow", "/var/log/auth.log",
    "/.ssh/id_", "/.ssh/authorized_keys",
    "/.aws/credentials", "/.aws/config",
    "/.azure/", "/.config/gcloud/",
    "/.kube/config", "/.docker/config.json",
    "/.env", "wallet.dat", "/.bitcoin/", "/.ethereum/keystore/", "/.solana/", "/.cardano/", "/Ledger/"
  ]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileAccessed")
   or ActionType has "File"
| extend MatchedPath = tostring(SensitivePaths[0])
| extend Hits = array_length(set_intersect(SensitivePaths, pack_array(FolderPath)))
| where FolderPath has_any (SensitivePaths) or FileName has_any ("shadow","auth.log","credentials","kubeconfig","wallet.dat")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp),
            DistinctSensitivePaths=dcount(FolderPath),
            PathsSample=make_set(FolderPath, 25),
            Cmd=any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId
| where DistinctSensitivePaths >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in ("auth","authpriv","daemon","user","kern")
| where ProcessName matches regex @"(?i)^python[0-9]?$"
   or SyslogMessage has_any ("python","python3")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/etc/shadow","/var/log/auth.log","/.ssh/id_","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.azure/","/.config/gcloud/","/.kube/config","/.docker/config.json","wallet.dat","/.bitcoin/","/.ethereum/keystore/","169.254.169.254")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated),
            Hits=count(),
            DistinctIndicators=dcount(extract(@"(/etc/shadow|/var/log/auth\.log|/\.ssh/id_|/\.aws/credentials|/\.aws/config|/\.azure/|/\.config/gcloud/|/\.kube/config|/\.docker/config\.json|wallet\.dat|/\.bitcoin/|/\.ethereum/keystore/|169\.254\.169\.254)", 0, SyslogMessage)),
            Sample=any(SyslogMessage),
            Procs=make_set(ProcessName)
          by Computer, HostName
| where DistinctIndicators >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(PATH OR EXECVE) @process.name:(python OR python3) (@file.path:(/etc/shadow OR /var/log/auth.log OR */.ssh/id_* OR */.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.azure/* OR */.config/gcloud/* OR */.kube/config OR */.docker/config.json OR */.env OR */wallet.dat OR */.bitcoin/* OR */.ethereum/keystore/*) OR @process.command_line:(*\/etc\/shadow* OR *\/var\/log\/auth.log* OR *169.254.169.254*))
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2)
| (ContextImageFileName=/python(3)?$/i OR ImageFileName=/python(3)?$/i)
| (TargetFileName=/\/etc\/shadow$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/var\/log\/auth\.log$/i OR TargetFileName=/\.ssh\/id_/i OR TargetFileName=/\.aws\/(credentials|config)$/i OR TargetFileName=/\.azure\//i OR TargetFileName=/\.config\/gcloud\//i OR TargetFileName=/\.kube\/config$/i OR TargetFileName=/\.docker\/config\.json$/i OR TargetFileName=/wallet\.dat$/i OR TargetFileName=/\.ethereum\/keystore/i OR CommandLine=/169\.254\.169\.254/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true), limit=200)
| _count >= 3
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3") AND (Filesystem.file_path="/etc/shadow" OR Filesystem.file_path="/var/log/auth.log" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.env" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/wallet.dat" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.bitcoin/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ethereum/keystore/*") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | stats min(firstTime) as firstTime values(paths) as touched_paths dc(file_path) as distinct_sensitive_paths by host user process_name | where distinct_sensitive_paths >= 3 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3") AND (Filesystem.file_path="/etc/shadow" OR Filesystem.file_path="/var/log/auth.log" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.env" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/wallet.dat" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.bitcoin/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ethereum/keystore/*") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | stats min(firstTime) as firstTime values(paths) as touched_paths dc(file_path) as distinct_sensitive_paths by host user process_name | where distinct_sensitive_paths >= 3 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| sort - count

ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email

     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
